thread:
maria: Quick sync — we've been seeing a small but consistent perf regression under high KV cache pressure. P95 latency spikes and a handful of soft OOMs during heavy prefix workloads. I want to propose a lightweight 'mem-scarcity adaptive batcher' heuristic and get quick feedback before I open a PR.

maria: Problem summary: when free KV bytes drop below ~120MB on an instance, admission keeps letting large-token requests in and we end up trimming batches mid-generation to avoid OOM, which causes kernel fallback thrash and higher latency.

maria: Proposal sketch: 1) compute an estimated KV footprint per request (kv_est). 2) maintain a moving min free_bytes estimate per GPU. 3) translate free_bytes into a token_budget ceiling for new admissions. 4) if request.tokens + kv_est > token_budget, either cap tokens we admit or route to slower model variant.

ajay: Do you have numbers for the regression? p50/p95 before vs after? Also how much error in kv_est are we tolerating?

maria: Quick profiling attached inline:
```
baseline (no pressure): p50=12ms, p95=62ms, soft_oom=0
under pressure (current admission): p50=14ms, p95=180ms, soft_oom=5/hour
with proto budget-cap (simulated): p50=13ms, p95=85ms, soft_oom=0-1/hour
```
kv_est error: currently we use a conservative estimate = max(approx_kv_size, 1.25 * observed_prefix_kv). Err on the side of overestimating to avoid OOM.

dave: Two quick notes: (1) mid-batch trimming is the killer because it forces fallback kernel that can't use the KV cache efficiently. (2) can we surface a metric 'admitted_tokens_vs_budget' so we know how often we hit the cap?

maria: yes to both. metric + alert in rollout plan. Also included a tiny pseudocode patch for the admission decision:
```
# admission heuristic (simplified)
free = gpu.free_kv_bytes_est
kv_est = estimate_kv_for(req)
budget_tokens = token_budget_from(free)  # maps free bytes -> token ceiling
if req.tokens + kv_est <= budget_tokens:
  admit_full(req)
else:
  if req.is_latency_sensitive:
    admit_trimmed(min(req.tokens, budget_tokens - kv_est))
  else:
    route_to_fallback_variant(req)
```

lenka: How does this interact with tenant fairness and rate limits? If budget_token is small we might starve low-priority but latency-sensitive tenants. We need per-tenant shares considered in mapping.

maria: good call. plan is: compute budget_tokens per GPU, then slice that into tenant shares by current quota weight. Budget mapping becomes: token_budget = global_budget * tenant_share. I'll add that.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: canary cluster baseline health shows 2x increase in soft-oom events after last runtime change (logs attached). Recommend hold new rollout until admission tweak tested.

maria: Thanks infra-bot. That's precisely why I want a conservative cap first, feature-flagged. Rollout plan: feature flag off by default, enable 1 rack canary (non-prod tenants), collect metrics for 48h: evictions/sec, soft_oom_count, admitted_tokens_vs_budget, tail_latency, kernel_fallback_rate. If stable, ramp to prod.

ajay: Also consider integrating kernel-selection signal: if we trim tokens due to KV budget, prefer the quantized kernel path or a kernel that avoids allocating extra temp KV structs. That reduces fallback churn.

maria: yep adding a kernel hint API to admission (admission -> preferred_kernel) in my TODOs.

dave: Test plan idea: synthetic workload generator that varies prefix lengths and issues a mix of small/large token requests. Run on a single GPU with artificial KV pressure (reserve memory) to validate token_budget curve.

maria: exactly what I had in mind. I'll spin up a bench job and drop numbers in this thread when I have them. Thanks for quick feedback. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident summary: last 24h had 3 soft OOM incidents attributed to batcher trimming loop on cluster-prod-7. Linked tickets: INC-4921, INC-4923.

maria: ack. I'll prioritize the bench and a small PR that implements the conservative token cap + metrics. Will ping when PR is ready for review.

lenka: please make sure the flag can be toggled per-rack and that the metrics include tenant breakdown.

maria: will do, adding those to the PR description.
